scope: Read-only audit of exact-head hosted/native/C evidence. source_scope_proof.arm_report:
# One-axis SIMD subpixel statistics

Native Apple M4 Max, Go1.27.2 archsimd, PGO off, GOMAXPROCS1. Parent eb820478,
old assembly691cd051. This is an immediate-parent comparison, not a comparison
with the earlier PR35 source. Skip an identity bilinear stage, retaining both
original extra-row/column endpoint checks and read-only alias semantics.
The bounded dispatcher proves w/h<=64, w%16==0 and nonnegative strides<2^30.
Every pointer offset is below2^36+64 and each exact load reads16bytes.

ARM uses wrapping int16 multiply-add, separate per-tile narrow difference sums,
independent int32 squared-error sums and paired rows with an odd-row tail.
Even arbitrary int16 coefficients produce a rounded stage in[-256,255]; the
removed identity stage maps that entire range exactly to itself. Differences
are[-511,255], so each separate lane sum over64rows lies[-32704,16320]. Widen
each half before merging. Total SSE<=1,069,551,616 and |sum|<=2,093,056 fit
signedint32. AMD uses one AVX2 packet and retains deferred upper-state cleanup.
Neither input is written or retained. CPU-off and other geometry/filters keep
their original fallbacks. Phase checks precede axis setup to protect controls.

Fresh six balanced parent/assembly/current permutations,100ms per40 public
fixtures, all zero B/op/allocations. Identical B.Loop fixtures, independent
per-pixel two-rounding scalar variance/SSE checks, unaligned3/5 origins, exact
visible spans, minimal/unequal padded strides and full backing canaries.

| One-axis fixture | Parent/current time | Assembly/current time | Minimum paired parent/current |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16x8/phase3-0/paddedfalse | 1.4805x | 2.1805x | 1.4733x |
| 16x8/phase3-0/paddedtrue | 1.4778x | 2.1776x | 1.4741x |
| 16x8/phase0-5/paddedfalse | 1.5344x | 2.2659x | 1.5131x |
| 16x8/phase0-5/paddedtrue | 1.5359x | 2.2986x | 1.5244x |
| 16x16/phase3-0/paddedfalse | 1.4286x | 0.9197x | 1.4164x |
| 16x16/phase3-0/paddedtrue | 1.4400x | 0.9273x | 1.4324x |
| 16x16/phase0-5/paddedfalse | 1.4874x | 0.9555x | 1.4821x |
| 16x16/phase0-5/paddedtrue | 1.4934x | 0.9583x | 1.4796x |
| 32x16/phase3-0/paddedfalse | 1.4373x | 1.3551x | 1.3987x |
| 32x16/phase3-0/paddedtrue | 1.4410x | 1.3511x | 1.4291x |
| 32x16/phase0-5/paddedfalse | 1.4917x | 1.3997x | 1.4417x |
| 32x16/phase0-5/paddedtrue | 1.4824x | 1.3794x | 1.4523x |
| 16x32/phase3-0/paddedfalse | 1.4388x | 1.0387x | 1.4257x |
| 16x32/phase3-0/paddedtrue | 1.4431x | 1.0375x | 1.4288x |
| 16x32/phase0-5/paddedfalse | 1.4996x | 1.0822x | 1.4855x |
| 16x32/phase0-5/paddedtrue | 1.4991x | 1.0826x | 1.4842x |

The two vertical16x8 fixtures qualify independently of whole-codec results:
all12 paired samples exceed 1.5131x parent.
Other one-axis results and every slower control remain in the summaries/raw
logs; do not round a sub1.5 result into a qualifying gain. The24 identity/two-axis
controls range 0.9947–1.0169x parent.
Some sizes still trail assembly; this is not a blanket assembly-parity claim.

Whole synthetic720p VP8,realtime CPU8,2500kbps,one thread, six balanced rounds:

* 300frames: -0.0246% time versus parent (4/6 faster), +4.3681% versus assembly (0/6 faster).

* 60frames: +0.0005% time versus parent (3/6 faster), +11.5610% versus assembly (0/6 faster).

All23 non-timing fields match and every allocation sample is zero. Six fixed
speed packet/drop digests match the validated parent exactly. Preserve the
verified >=1.5x component gain even if whole-codec performance is unchanged;
the overall ARM assembly gap remains open. Shared-desktop timings and varied
assembly samples do not justify causal/additive claims across checkpoints.

Validation includes the full final native suite, dispatcher-focused tests,
ARM race/checkptr2, AMD correctness/checkptr under
Rosetta, actual AVX-off fallback, independent arithmetic/bounds/alias/dispatch
review, refreshed PGO and repository gates. New coverage includes864 wrapped
coefficient/alias/stride/shape cases,48 short-window cases and40 directed narrow
sum boundary cases including h65 fallback and w48 three-packet geometry.
All64 legal public phases and existing numeric extremes pass scalar oracles.
Selected root/prototype generated-code evidence and final source hashes remain
with the raw logs. Native x64 speed awaits the successor's exact-head CI.

The archive retains every diagnostic, all six rounds, all outliers, the earlier
qualifying unrolled checkpoint, unselected weighted-row cache/shift/multiply
variants and source/driver snapshots. The first packet-digest command matched
no tests; its warning is retained, then the explicit fixture was copied and
six real digests verified. No concurrent local builds/profiles during timing.
README files, dependencies and handwritten-assembly production policy remain
unchanged. No production cgo added.

pr_snapshot.body:
One-axis motion still executes both bilinear stages. Add one-pass Go SIMD statistics for bounded 16-column tiles when either phase is identity, retaining both original input-window checks, int16 wrapping, read-only aliases and fallbacks. ARM pairs rows with proven int16 difference sums; x64 uses AVX2 and retains upper-state cleanup. Check phases first so ordinary two-axis work skips setup.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go1.27.2, PGO off, six fresh balanced parent/assembly/current rounds over 40 public fixtures:

- The two vertical-only 16×8 fixtures improve **1.534–1.536× versus parent `eb820478`**; all 12 paired samples exceed **1.513×**. They beat old assembly **2.266–2.299×**.
- The other identity/two-axis controls range **0.995–1.017× parent**. Every slower sample is preserved; some larger one-axis sizes still trail assembly.
- Whole synthetic VP8 720p is effectively flat: **−0.0246% time over 300 frames**, **+0.0005% over 60**, with all 23 non-timing fields exact and zero allocations. Assembly still takes less time on these ARM workloads. Keep the correctness-verified ≥1.5× component win independently of whole-codec timing, as required by AGENTS.md.

Parent `eb820478` and merged main `98302461` have identical trees. Full final native suite, scalar/all-phase oracles, 864 unusual-coefficient/alias cases, 48 short-window cases, 40 narrow-sum boundary cases, ARM race/checkptr2, x64 correctness/checkptr and AVX-off fallback pass. All six fixed-speed packet/drop digests match. Selected ARM instruction words match the measured prototype; PGO/fingerprint/noasm/SIMD-selection/pre-commit gates pass.

Native Intel Xeon 8370C measurements of predecessor `1e8809b6` exposed four vertical cases **21–47% slower than main in every pair**. The current repair carries widened AVX2 rows, eliminating a legacy SSE hot-loop copy in the saved optimized x64 build and one repeated widening. Arithmetic and cleanup are unchanged; ARM and x64 horizontal code are unchanged. Correctness/checkptr and repository gates pass. The corrected exact head now passes all three CI checks and the fresh native audit below; the earlier regression remains separately scoped. All predecessor results, including the regressions and the separately scoped C comparison, are preserved in the [predecessor report](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/blob/f3a02aee81979d0c822f5814343f2287d9d86194/benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-amd64/2026-10-18-one-axis-predecessor/REPORT.md).

Require the new axis tests in native and race/checkptr preflight, record nine source hashes, and retain all 246 existing identical native fixtures. Native x64 and optimized-C results for this exact head are complete below. Rosetta remains correctness-only.

Preserve complete benchmark/source archives and PR36’s independently scoped native/C audits, including every regression. README files and dependencies stay clean.

[ARM measurements and proof](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/blob/1e8809b63498b77fb6a347b0c085ebfe3c9aab49/benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-arm64/2026-10-18-subpel-axis/REPORT.md) · [Merged PR36 x64/C audit](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/blob/1e8809b63498b77fb6a347b0c085ebfe3c9aab49/benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-amd64/2026-10-18-pr36-subpel-identity/audit.json)

Final corrected-head evidence for `f3a02aee` (Go 1.27.2, PGO off):

- On **EPYC 7763**, all **16 one-axis fixtures are faster than main and old ASM in every paired sample**. Horizontal medians are **1.206–1.382× main / 2.785–3.541× ASM**; vertical medians **1.248–1.474× main / 2.968–3.653× ASM**. No AMD fixture reaches 1.5× main here; retain the independently qualifying ARM gain without relabeling it. Do not infer a numerical repair speedup from predecessor measurements on Intel.
- All **246 kernels × six samples × three variants** allocate zero bytes/objects. Nine source hashes match; **109 targeted checks / 254 PASS lines** include the axis tests under selected SIMD and race/checkptr, with no failures/skips. All 22 semantic fields and every public/profile allocation sample match; no allocation outlier.
- Whole VP8 time is **−2.0738% versus main** (5/6 pairs faster), **−21.6138% versus ASM**. VP9 320 is **−0.0157% versus main** (4/6) / **−39.8709% versus ASM**; VP9 720 **−0.7230% versus main** (4/6) / **−47.0425% versus ASM**. These results remain CPU/job scoped; no prior 9V74 gap-closure or isolated causal claim.
- Preserve **all 111 median regressions and 75 all-six-slower kernels**. Unchanged controls include Variance16x16 +10.668%, slice-SAD early +5.259–5.540%, Split8x4 +3.779% and several gather8 cases around +2.73–2.86%. Two-axis controls range **0.979–1.011× main**, including slowdowns. Identity controls range **1.006–1.142×**. Every raw pair and output/allocation control remains included.
- Optimized libvpx runs separately on **EPYC 9V45**. Fixed-speed VP8 Go takes **2.114012× libvpx time** (+111.4012%; libvpx is faster), with matched measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/frame counts, without claiming bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 +48.8166% and VP9 +168.2170%/+168.7046% perform unequal quality/output work. **Adaptive C timed payloads include 678205 and 685355 bytes while the quality pass produces 678205**, so its quality metrics do not represent every timed payload. Other quality-pass output statistics match their timing outputs. All reference timers use `vpxenc-stats`; pinned ASM/SSE2/AVX2/runtime dispatch are enabled. Never combine native and C host timings.

The final archive preserves 86 native + 74 C raw files byte for byte, with audit and SHA256 manifests, alongside the rejected predecessor data. The stacked SSE PR is retargeted to main only after this squash merge is proven to have the tested tree; no local checkout/index changes.

limits: Kernel gains do not imply whole-codec gains or blanket assembly parity.
Compare native main/ASM/current only within this CPU/job; separate C host timings and unequal quality/work retained explicitly.
Every median regression/all-six-slower kernel and allocation exception retained, no sample pruning.
Fixed VP8 matching measured quality/payload/counts does not prove bitstream identity.
Root reviewed final audit and authorized guarded remote merge; local checkout/index/branches untouched.

diff --git a/internal/pixel/subpel_axis_amd64.go b/internal/pixel/subpel_axis_amd64.go
index cee8df90..9fa477ca 100644
--- a/internal/pixel/subpel_axis_amd64.go
+++ b/internal/pixel/subpel_axis_amd64.go
@@ -30,6 +30,9 @@ func subpelStatsAxisHorizontal16(src []byte, ss int, ref []byte, rs, w, h int, f
 	}
 	return int(sum32(sum.GetLo().Add(sum.GetHi()))), uint32(sum32(sse.GetLo().Add(sse.GetHi())))
 }
+
+// Keep the rolling row widened: a byte-vector phi can lower to a legacy SSE
+// register copy inside the AVX2 loop and cause transitions on native x64.
 func subpelStatsAxisVertical16(src []byte, ss int, ref []byte, rs, w, h int, f [2]int16) (int, uint32) {
 	sp, rp := unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(src)), unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(ref))
 	defer archsimd.ClearAVXUpperBits()
@@ -37,12 +40,12 @@ func subpelStatsAxisVertical16(src []byte, ss int, ref []byte, rs, w, h int, f [
 	var sum, sse archsimd.Int32x8
 	for x := 0; x < w; x += 16 {
 		so, ro := x, x
-		a := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(sp, x)))
+		a := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(sp, x))).ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16()
 		so += ss
 		for range h {
-			b := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(sp, so)))
+			b := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(sp, so))).ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16()
 			r := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(rp, ro)))
-			v := a.ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16().Mul(f0).Add(b.ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16().Mul(f1)).Add(round).ShiftAllRight(7)
+			v := a.Mul(f0).Add(b.Mul(f1)).Add(round).ShiftAllRight(7)
 			d := v.Sub(r.ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16())
 			sum = sum.Add(d.DotProductPairs(ones))
 			sse = sse.Add(d.DotProductPairs(d))
repair_scope.change: AMD vertical rolling row is widened to Int16x16 once at load; avoid legacySSE byte-vector phi whileYMMlive. Same filter arithmetic/window/AVXcleanup. ARM and AMDhorizontal source unchanged.
repair_scope.interpretation: Compiled codegen is a mechanism hypothesis; this exact-head native comparison versus main determines performance, not prior CPU/job timing.
